title: BBC Proms 2015, Prom 49
subtitle: Hardenberger, Burton-Hill, Rolfs · Nelsons
summary: Off-air recording of the BBC Radio 3 live broadcast of BBC Proms 2015 Prom 49, Royal Albert Hall, London, Saturday 22 August 2015: Andris Nelsons conducts the Boston Symphony Orchestra in Brett Dean's trumpet concerto Dramatis personae (soloist Håkan Hardenberger) and Mahler's Symphony No. 6, presented by Clemency Burton-Hill. This was the first concert of the BSO's 2015 European tour.
date_evidence: Folder '150822 Prom 49' = 2015-08-22. The Royal Albert Hall catalogue record (PERF11527, re-read by the reconciler) gives Performance Date 22 August 2015, 18:35, Prom 49, 'Broadcast live on BBC Radio 3.' The BBC programme page b066zjlk (re-read) says 'Live from the Royal Albert Hall' with broadcast Sat 22 Aug 2015 18:30, and the Radio 3 listings PDF for 22-28 Aug 2015 (re-read) gives SAT 18:30 (part 1) and SAT 19:25 (part 2). Reviews dated to the night agree: Seen and Heard '22.8.2015', Bachtrack 'Reviewed at Royal Albert Hall, London on 22 August 2015', Boston Globe 'Saturday night', The Arts Desk (23 Aug) 'last night'. The BBC also lists a repeat on Mon 7 Sep 2015 at 2pm. The folder date points to the live 22 Aug transmission, but this is not verified from the audio.

program.title: Dramatis personae, for trumpet and orchestra
program.notes: Composed 2013 for Håkan Hardenberger; first performance at the Proms. Three movements: I. Fall of a Superhero; II. Soliloquy; III. The Accidental Revolutionary. The BBC gives a duration of c28 min. No Wikidata item was found.

program.title: Symphony No. 6 in A minor 'Tragic'
program.notes: Played after the interval with the Scherzo second and the Andante third. Seen and Heard ('Nelsons chose to put the Scherzo second'), The Arts Desk, the Boston Globe and Classical Iconoclast all report this order. Seen and Heard: 'there was no encore.'

credits.notes: Named in the exact-date RAH archive record, the BBC broadcast pages and listing, and every review of the night. No change of conductor is reported anywhere.

The RAH record lists 'Hakan Hardenberger - trumpet'. The Boston Globe says the concerto was 'performed by soloist Hakan Hardenberger', and The Arts Desk comments on his playing that night. No substitution is reported.

'Presented by Clemency Burton-Hill' appears on BBC programme page b066zjlk (re-read by the reconciler) and on the Radio 3 listings PDF for both parts of the 22 Aug broadcast (re-read). These are broadcast-day listings and the voice was not checked against the audio. A presenter change on the night is possible but nothing suggests one.

Only the Claude researcher reported this credit. The reconciler re-read the Boston Globe review of the night: 'When principal trumpet player Thomas Rolfs stood to take a solo bow after a stellar night in the Mahler'. He is an orchestra member, not a billed soloist. No Wikidata QID was looked up.

open_questions: The BBC Proms Performance Archive event page for 2015 Prom 49 was not found. The exact-date Royal Albert Hall archive record, the BBC broadcast pages and listings, and four reviews of the night all agree on the performers, and none reports a substitution.

The BBC lists a repeat on Mon 7 Sep 2015 at 2pm. The folder date 150822 points to the live 22 Aug broadcast, but the audio has not been checked. Since it is the same performance, only broadcast_date would change.

Track boundaries and the contents of the spoken and applause tracks (01, 03, 04, 09) are inferred from durations and the schedule, not from listening. Tracks 03-04 total only about 8 minutes, so the 20-minute interval and its Proms Extra talk (The Lumière Brothers in 1895) appear to have been cut.

Track 02 (30:32) is about 2.5 minutes longer than the listed c28 minutes for Dramatis personae. It probably includes applause. Whether Hardenberger played an encore after the concerto is not documented; Seen and Heard's 'no encore' remark appears to refer to the end of the concert.
The presenter credit rests on broadcast-day listings and has not been checked against the voice on the recording.
No Wikidata item was found for Dean's Dramatis personae, and none was looked up for Thomas Rolfs.
The Wayback availability API returned no snapshots for the BBC programme pages, the RAH record or the reviews, apart from the Seen and Heard snapshot.
